title: extcap: Really don't load extcap interfaces if disabled
description:
If the capture.no_extcap preference is set, really don't load the
extcap interfaces. Previously, the extcap interfaces were loaded
before the preference was read, because otherwise the extcap
preferences wouldn't be registered and properly read out of the
configuration file.

Wait until after that preference is read to register the
extcap preferences and then re-read just the extcap module
preferences from the configuration files. Make sure to check
other times when the preference may be changed, such as
switching profiles.

Write extcap prefs to a separate file so that they don't get lost
if the extcap interfaces aren't loaded and the prefs are then
written out. Continue writing them to the main file for backwards
compability.

Related to #15295. Cuts ~100 ms off the loading time of Wireshark
in a normal situation if the capture.no_extcap preference is set,
more if an extcap has some kind of issue that makes it take a long
time to load.

[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/14436/diffs?diff_id=928233890&start_sha=f1a4c4135c78acd711766a50733840f438bd140c)

Earlier we had the `extcap` folder in ~/.config/wireshark, and users may still have this. I do. When this exists you will get a warning, both on read and write. After visiting preferences, writing "extcap" will fail and you end up with an empty "preferences" file.

**At startup:**

![Screenshot_2024-02-19_at_23.06.22](/uploads/000e3aab6db57fe0503e662a1ce8e468/Screenshot_2024-02-19_at_23.06.22.png)

**After visiting preferences:**

![Screenshot_2024-02-20_at_08.41.44](/uploads/e24ee10fe1d807d02170194a0683e7cc/Screenshot_2024-02-20_at_08.41.44.png)

First things off, I'll make it write the main prefs file no matter what.

We might still write the extcap directory on some platforms if someone isn't running with a profile, so that name might not work. I'll check for if it's a directory now and do nothing, but maybe a different name than just the module name would be a better idea, like "extcap.cfg" or something?

`copy_persconffile_profile()` only checks if a file that has been added to profile_files exists, and it fails with an error on directories. It also fails even worse if a filename exists but is a FIFO.

+/** Given a module name, read the preferences associated with only that module.
+ * Checks for a file in the personal configuration directory named after the
+ * module first.
+ *
+ * @param name The preference module name, e.g. "extcap".
+ */
+WS_DLL_PUBLIC
+void
+prefs_read_module(const char *name);
+
 WS_DLL_PUBLIC
 gboolean
 prefs_pref_is_default(pref_t *pref);
